--- title: Coordinate transformations and field line tracing subtitle: GeoCotrans.jl compared with IRBEM and PySPEDAS engine: julia --- [GeoCotrans.jl](https://juliaspacephysics.github.io/GeoCotrans.jl/dev/) is a native Julia implementation of geocentric coordinate transformations and IGRF field line tracing. Here we check it against [IRBEM.jl](https://juliaspacephysics.github.io/IRBEM.jl/dev/) (Fortran) and [PySPEDAS](https://github.com/spedas/pyspedas) (Python), and benchmark the three. ::: {.callout-note} ## Takeaway GeoCotrans agrees closely with IRBEM and PySPEDAS and is an order of magnitude faster. It interpolates IGRF coefficients and the Sun's direction more finely, which accounts for the small differences. ::: ::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using GeoCotrans, IRBEM using PySPEDAS, PySPEDAS.PythonCall using DimensionalData, Dates, Chairmarks, Test using OrdinaryDiffEqTsit5 irbem_cotrans(pos, in, out) = coord_trans(in, out, collect(dims(pos, Ti)), parent(pos)')' ``` ::: THEMIS-A positions from the [PySPEDAS test cases](https://github.com/spedas/pyspedas/blob/master/pyspedas/cotrans_tools/tests/test_cotrans.py): ::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} @py import pyspedas.cotrans_tools.tests.test_cotrans: CotransTestCases CotransTestCases().test_cotrans() pyspedas.projects.themis.state(["2010-02-25/00:00:00", "2010-02-25/23:59:59"], probe = "a", time_clip = true) tha_pos = set(DimArray(PySPEDAS.get_data("tha_pos")), Dim{:time} => Ti) tha_pos_gse = set(DimArray(PySPEDAS.get_data("tha_pos_gse")), Dim{:time} => Ti) ``` ::: ## Agreement ::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} jl = gei2geo(tha_pos) py = PySPEDAS.get_data("tha_pos_new_geo") @test jl ≈ parent(py) @test jl ≈ irbem_cotrans(tha_pos, "GEI", "GEO") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}
